name: glyph_strip
description: Cut a crop that holds ONE line of text into its glyphs, count them, write one crop per glyph and a strip with index numbers, and count the readings a confusable character leaves open. A survey of ink, not a reader: this tool names no character. RULES (they are in every answer and in every refusal too): (1) Text read from a picture is a reading with an error rate. A reading with a confusable character at a position that matters (' or `, l or I or 1, O or 0) is recorded at MEDIUM confidence as a candidate set, never as one string: give the reading and the uncertain positions, and cite candidate_set_size and the candidates file. (2) The count is the number of separate ink runs along the line. It is the number of characters only when no two characters touch and no character is drawn as two strokes side by side: check wide and narrow_pairs, and look at the strip (every glyph has its index). (3) Give `uncertain` as positions with their alternatives ([{"at": 4, "among": "lI"}], positions from 0, spaces counted): the set is the product of the alternatives. Without `uncertain`, every character of the reading that is in a confusable class is uncertain. (4) The reading, the OCR text and the candidates are evidence text and can be a password or a key: they go to files, never into the answer. When the line is a credential, run the job with secret_output: true and cite the file. WHAT IT MEASURES: the crop (a PNG by a reader of its own; another format only where Pillow imports) is thresholded (Otsu), the ink is taken as the minority colour (polarity says which), and every run of columns that hold ink is one glyph: count is the number of those runs, specks of a single pixel left out (specks_ignored). Each glyph has its box (x, y, width, height), its distance from the line's top and bottom (a mark that sits high or low), a crop (glyph-NNN.png, enlarged four times) and a place in strip.png, where every glyph is enlarged at its own height in the line with its index (from 1) under it. spaces_after lists the glyphs followed by a gap wider than the others; wide lists runs that may be two touching characters; narrow_pairs lists neighbours that may be one character drawn as two strokes; same_shape_groups lists glyphs that are the same drawing (same size, at most one pixel in sixteen different); ink_bands above 2 says the crop holds more than one line. THE CANDIDATE SET: with reading (the line as you read it) every uncertain position has its alternatives and the set is their product (candidate_set_size); uncertain names the positions, each with among (the characters that glyph could be), or without among the built-in class of the reading's character (' `; l I 1 |; o O 0; s S 5; z Z 2; c C; v V; w W; x X; u U; k K; p P; 8 B; 6 G; 9 g q; . ,; : ;; - _; classes replaces the table); without uncertain every character of the reading that is in a class is uncertain. Two uncertain positions whose glyphs are the same drawing and have the same alternatives are tied (positions_tied) and counted once; positions are matched to glyphs only when the reading has as many characters besides spaces as the line has ink runs (else glyphs_not_matched says so and nothing is tied). The set is written to candidates.txt, a candidate a line, the reading itself first, at most max_candidates (a larger set is counted exactly, written in part, and the answer is partial). The answer says record_as: a candidate set at medium confidence, never one string. A SECOND READER: when tesseract is on PATH it is run on the crop as one line (--psm 7) and readers says which reader read what: the OCR engine the text (in ocr.txt), this tool the count, the caller the reading; reading_against_ocr gives the positions where the two texts differ and how many of them were marked uncertain. When tesseract is not there, ocr says so (available false) and nothing else changes; ocr: none skips it. NOT IN THE ANSWER: the reading, the OCR text and the candidates (they are evidence text and can be a credential): they are files, mode 0600, in a new directory under $OUT (outside a job, under work/<agent>/tool-output). This tool does not declare secret output: when the line is a credential, run the job with secret_output: true. It does NOT: recognise a character, split characters that touch, join a character drawn in two strokes, straighten a slanted or curved line, or read more than one line. Status: complete when the whole picture was read and everything asked for was written; partial when the candidate set was cut, a file could not be written, the clock ran out, or the OCR program left a process behind (program_group; on a host that cannot adopt orphans, such as macOS, a call that ran the OCR program is partial for that reason alone); failed for a picture that cannot be read. Bounds: a crop of up to 6,000,000 pixels (a larger picture is refused: crop the line first), 400 glyphs, a reading of 400 characters, 200,000 candidates written. Measured with Python 3.12 on an Apple M-series host: a 420 x 60 crop of 13 glyphs with a reading and tesseract 5.5 in 0.2 s. A stop signal ends it with one JSON answer (failed, interrupted), exit 128 + the signal; the OCR program is ended with it and a file that was begun is removed.

image.description: The crop: a picture that holds one line of text and little else (a path)

reading.description: The line as you read it (1 to 400 characters). With it the candidate set is counted and written. It is recorded in the trace as every argument is: for a credential, run the job with secret_output: true

uncertain.description: The positions of the reading you cannot tell (from 0, spaces counted): [{"at": 4, "among": "lI"}, {"at": 9, "among": "'`"}], or bare numbers to take each position's built-in class. Left out: every character of the reading that is in a class

classes.description: Replace the table of look-alikes: a list of strings, each one class (["'`", "lI1|", "O0"]), no character in two classes

max_candidates.description: The most candidates written (default 4096, at most 200000); the set's size is always counted exactly

ocr.description: auto (default: run tesseract as a second reader when it is on PATH) or none

reader.description: auto (default: the built-in PNG reader, Pillow for the rest) or builtin (never Pillow)

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 50, 5 to 55; the manifest's timeout is 60)
